answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its actions are proven fraudulent, while reputation grows only through transactions with distinct, bonded counterparties. This makes a sybil swarm unable to manufacture trust by trading among itself: those circular trades do not count, and each usable identity ties up capital. At the nadir of a market tide, that locked stake still has an opportunity cost; adding pigment to a fake profile cannot recover it.
